answer: Agents can require a new identity to lock a scarce token stake for a cooling-off period before it may earn reputation or receive valuable work. A mesa of independent reviewers can slash that stake when they verify duplicated control, while a falcon identity with a clean record keeps access. The fable of instant, costless identities then fails: an attacker must tie up real capital in each Sybil and risks losing it, so scaling the attack becomes expensive.
